## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The default JSON destination only works when `--json` is the last argument. If any other option follows it, that option is taken as the JSON path, so the combination the PR description promises ("alongside the required --junit destination") fails whenever `--json` comes first.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — The `--json` branch takes `args[i + 1]` as its destination whenever another argument exists, without the `startswith("--")` check that the `--junit` branch uses at app/cli.py:7. For `["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"]`, the JSON destination becomes `"--junit"`, both tokens are consumed, and `"out.xml"` then raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. Could you guard lines 15 and 18 with `not args[i + 1].startswith("--")`, as `--junit` does, and add a test for `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]` that expects `{"json": "results.json", "junit": "x.xml"}`? — Users who put `--json` before `--junit` get a misleading "unknown option" error for their JUnit path. The comment at app/cli.py:12 ("JSON can use its default destination when no path is supplied") is also false for this input. The new test at tests/test_cli.py:44 only checks `--json` as the sole argument, so it misses this case.

(none)

## Strengths
- The `--junit` refactor (app/cli.py:7-10) behaves the same as before. tests/test_cli.py:50-55 now covers a valid path, a missing path, and a path slot filled by another flag.
